notes: Seed engine: flat-shaded boxes and cones painted on a 2D canvas.

narration: Darkness, soft and windless, and then a pressure under your feet: ground. It is pale grey stone, cool and faintly gritty, spreading out a few paces in every direction before the dark swallows it. Far to the north, low down, a single small light flickers, warm as an ember.

facts.description: A flat plain of pale grey, slightly gritty stone, fading into darkness about 15 m out in every direction.
facts.placement: underfoot, centered on the wanderer, radius about 15 m

facts.description: A tiny warm orange light, like a lantern or ember, flickering gently, about 1 m above the ground.
facts.placement: about 40 m north of the wanderer

notes: I laid a pale grey slab 30 m wide under the Wanderer and set the ground beyond it to near-black, so the stone fades into the dark. A small orange box floats 40 m north as the distant light. It can't flicker in this engine.

critique: Right now it's a grey slab in a black void, with one orange pixel in the distance. That's honest to the story, but the ground is a flat, harsh grey that looks like a paper cutout. The ember is the only point of interest, so I'm steering toward warmth against cold darkness, with lighting as the first big leap.

suggestions.change: Recolor to a cooler, darker stone #5d6068 so it reads as dim stone in the dark rather than a bright tile. Keep size 30,0.05,30.
Set sky to #05060c and ground to #05050a so the plain fades seamlessly into the void.
Make the ember a little more visible: size 0.6,0.6,0.6, color #ffb347, at [0,1,-40].
Add a tiny warm glow base under the ember: box id ember_glow at [0,0.05,-40], size 3,0.02,3, color #3a2412. It fakes a pool of light on the ground within the budget.

styleGuide: Palette: void #05060c, cool stone #5d6068, ember orange #ffb347, warm glow #3a2412, skin/wood browns #8a6a3e. engineRequest: Build a tiny WebGL (or fast canvas) renderer in about 4 KB that replaces flat 2D boxes. It should draw real 3D with a perspective camera behind the Wanderer. It needs per-face shading from one directional light plus ambient, distance fog fading to the sky color, and point lights (position, color, radius) with flicker. The ground should be lit by the ember with a falloff pool. Keep the existing ops (set, del, sky, ground, move), and add `light` {at,color,radius,flicker}. Add a gentle vertical gradient sky. This makes the dark, ember-lit world atmospheric at once.

notes:
Engine v1 is a tiny WebGL renderer (about 3.7 KB with the migrated world; the check reports exactly 4.0 KB of 4.0 KB, so there is almost no room left). The 2D boxes become real 3D, seen through a perspective camera behind the Wanderer. Faces are shaded by a cool directional light plus ambient, distance fog fades everything into a gradient sky, and the ember's flickering light casts a warm falloff pool on the cold stone ground. The new `light` op adds more flickering point lights, up to four.

Migration keeps both story things. It brightens the ground so the ember pool shows, and it adds a light to the glowing distant ember.

The check passes and both preview pictures look right, but two things fell short:
- The Wanderer is quite dark and the ember is small. Fixing either would have pushed the build back over budget.
- The Builder has essentially no room to grow before the next engine. To fit, I dropped id-name validation on `set` and `light` and cut the flicker to one sine wave.

I recolored the stone pad to a cooler, dimmer grey, darkened the sky and ground so the plain fades into the void, and made the ember slightly bigger and warmer. I skipped the extra glow-base box because only 11 bytes were free, and the ember's own light already makes a warm pool.

thought: A lone ember of light in the dark north. It's the only thing here, so it must matter. I'll head toward it.
action: Walk north across the stone toward the flickering light.

narration: You walk north, your steps scuffing softly on the gritty stone. The edge of the grey plain slides past beneath you, and the ground goes on, now a dark cracked slate. Ahead, the ember resolves into a small lantern hanging from a crooked iron post, and beside it a low standing stone, tall as a child, catches its glow.
movement: walks about 25 m north across the grey plain and stops about 15 m south of the lantern post

facts.description: A crooked black iron post about 2 m tall, bent slightly to the east, with a small glass lantern hanging from its tip holding a warm orange flame. It replaces the floating ember.
facts.placement: about 15 m north of the wanderer, at the position of distant_light

facts.description: Dark blue-black slate paving with thin pale cracks, continuing the plain beyond the grey stone.
facts.placement: surrounds the wanderer, extending about 20 m in every direction from lantern_post

facts.description: A small weathered standing stone about 1 m tall, rough and pale grey, with a single carved spiral on its south face, lit orange by the lantern.

notes: I swapped the floating ember for a thin bent iron post with a glowing lantern. I added a pale standing stone beside it and darkened the ground to slate. Budget was tight, so the stone has no carved spiral and the slate has no cracks.

critique: The world is nearly black: the Wanderer is a dim brown block, the ground is a faint slab, and the lantern is a single orange pixel. The lighting works, but everything is too dark and too small to read, and the 4 KB budget leaves no room to build the lantern post, the standing stone or the slate. I'm asking for 16 KB so the lantern's warm pool can anchor the scene.

Beneath the lantern, the pale cracks in the slate run toward the post like roots, and past it, a faint line of small flat stones leads north into the dark.

facts.description: The standing stone, about 1 m tall and rough pale grey, with a deep worn spiral carved on its south face, lit orange.

notes: I laid a slate slab around the lantern with pale crack lines running out from its base. I carved the spiral as a dark patch on the stone's south face and set ten stepping stones north into the dark. With so little room, the cracks are just two straight crossing lines, not a true radial spread.

critique: The lantern now anchors the scene, but the Wanderer is a dull brown slab and the world is still too dark to read. The standing stone is a grey block with its spiral barely visible, and the pale cracks and stepping stones are thin lines lost in the gloom. I'm steering toward a brighter warm pool, readable silhouettes and a richer ground. I'm holding the 64 KB unlock until we've spent the 10 KB we have.

engineRequest: Engine v2 (must fit in about 12 KB with the world): keep every v1 op and add (1) a hemisphere ambient term, cool blue from above and warm bounce from below; (2) procedural noise on the ground and on stone albedo, so slate and granite look gritty; (3) shadows for the lantern light using a simple blob or projected shadow under each thing; (4) light-aware glow bloom, a soft halo around glow things; (5) a Wanderer drawn with a head and brighter, self-lit rim so the figure reads; (6) point-light flicker with two or three summed sines; (7) raise the point-light limit to 8; (8) restore id validation. Add a `rot` field to set (yaw degrees) so cracks and stepping stones can be angled. Priority: atmosphere and readability at this size.

thought: The spiral carving feels like a clue, and the stone in the picture looks like a small block with a dark hollow. I want to touch the spiral before heading on.
action: Trace the carved spiral on the standing stone with my fingers.

narration: You lay your fingers in the spiral's groove and follow it inward, the stone cold and smooth as river glass. At the center your fingertip finds a small round hollow, and the lantern's flame leans toward you, as if listening. Beneath your touch the stone hums faintly, and a thin line of orange light creeps outward along the groove, tracing the spiral back out and over the ground toward the stepping stones.

facts.description: The carved spiral on the standing stone now glows with thin molten-orange light along its groove, with a small round hollow, about 4 cm wide, at its center.
facts.placement: on the south face of standing_stone, about 2 m west of lantern_post

facts.description: A narrow line of glowing orange light, about 5 cm wide, running along the ground like a thin vein from the standing stone to the first of the stepping_stones.
facts.placement: starts at the base of standing_stone, passes east of lantern_post and runs about 6 m north to meet stepping_stones

facts.description: The crooked iron post's lantern flame now leans west toward the standing stone and burns slightly brighter.
facts.placement: about 2 m east of standing_stone, unchanged position

notes: I traced the spiral on the stone's south face with thin glowing orange strips and a tiny center hollow, then ran a glowing line east past the lantern post and north to the first stepping stone. The lantern flame now sits leaning west and burns brighter. The spiral is a squared-off simplification because the engine only has boxes.

critique: The lantern bloom now glows beautifully and the glowing light trail and cracks finally read as veins of fire on the slate. But the scene is still a few thin boxes on an empty plane: the Wanderer is hardly visible, the stone's spiral is lost, and the horizon is a flat line. I'm steering toward form and depth: more objects in the pool of light, a richer ground, and a taller silhouette against the glow. We have 8 KB free, so I'm spending it before asking for more.
